newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- focus on upcoming data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- focus on upcoming data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were flat in what was expected to be an extremely quiet Monday session, traders said.
"It's hard to get out of the shoot here," one trader said. "Bid lists are nil. There isn't any tone."
The trader said this week's data releases were about the only focus.

Key figures include June retail sales on Tuesday and the consumer price index on Wednesday. Economists surveyed by Reuters expected retail sales to show a 0.2 percent rise, and the overall CPI to have risen 0.2 percent.
Early Monday data included the Atlanta Fed's manufacturing index, which was 17.5 in June versus 17.3 in May. The prices paid index fell to 8.7 last month from 11.0 in May.
The long bond showed little movement after the data, however, and was down 8/32 at 101 to yield 6.55 percent.
Government securities began Monday lower on profit taking from last week's strong run-up. Those gains came amid new evidence that inflation was tame.
Standard & Poor's Blue List of secondary offerings dipped to $944 million Monday, from $1.057 billion on Friday.
In futures action Monday, September municipals lost 4/32 to 119-12/32, while September T-bonds shed 6/32 to 113-30/32. The MOB spread widened to 174 from 172 at the close on Thursday.
Municipal bond sales for this week were expected to total $2.507 billion in 122 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.780 billion in 47 sales, with a $350 million Los Angeles Unified School District offering through BancAmerica topping the list.
On the competitive side, 75 sales totaling $727 million are scheduled. A $78.5 million Virginia HDA offering on July 17 is the largest.
